program.source: export function evaluate({ inputs, time }) { const launchSpeed = inputs.launchSpeed; const gravity = 9.8; const t = time; const height = launchSpeed * t - 0.5 * gravity * t * t; const velocity = launchSpeed - gravity * t; const apexTime = launchSpeed / gravity; const apexHeight = (launchSpeed * launchSpeed) / (2 * gravity); const scaleY = 30; const baseY = 340; const ballY = baseY - height * scaleY; const ballX = 320; let motionState = "Moving up"; if (Math.abs(velocity) < 0.05) { motionState = "Still for an instant"; } else if (velocity < 0) { motionState = "Moving down"; } const gravityState = "Gravity pulls down"; const objects = []; objects.push(sdk.panel({ x: 40, y: 40, w: 560, h: 360, title: "Vertical Toss", state: motionState })); objects.push(sdk.axis("axis.height", { x: 120, y: 340, length: 280, orientation: "y", min: 0, max: 2.5, ticks: [0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5], label: "Height", unit: "m" })); objects.push(sdk.groundMark("ground", ballX, baseY, 60, "Launch")); objects.push(sdk.circle("ball.toss", ballX, Math.max(60, Math.min(baseY, ballY)), 24, { role: "output" })); if (Math.abs(velocity) >= 0.05) { objects.push(sdk.vector("vec.v", { x: ballX + 20, y: Math.max(60, Math.min(baseY, ballY)) }, { value: velocity, direction: "up" }, { scale: 10, minLength: 12, label: "v" })); } objects.push(sdk.vector("vec.a", { x: ballX - 20, y: Math.max(60, Math.min(baseY, ballY)) }, { value: -gravity, direction: "up" }, { scale: 5, minLength: 12, label: "a" })); objects.push(sdk.callout(ballX + 45, Math.max(60, Math.min(baseY, ballY)) - 20, [motionState, gravityState], { id: "callout.toss" })); return { frame: { width: 640, height: 420, objects: objects, readouts: [{ id: "motionState", value: motionState }, { id: "gravityState", value: gravityState }] }, quantities: { launchSpeed: launchSpeed, gravity: gravity, apexTime: apexTime, apexHeight: apexHeight, velocity: velocity, height: height } }; }

manifest.title: The ball stops rising. Gravity doesn’t stop.
manifest.summary: Gravity slows the ball on the way up and speeds it up on the way down, pulling continuously even at the apex.
manifest.description: A vertical height scale shows a ball tossed upward, slowing down, stopping briefly at the apex, and falling back down. A blue velocity arrow shrinks, disappears at the top, and points downward during descent, while a dashed gravity arrow remains constant.
manifest.instructions: Change launch speed, then press Play. At the top, playback pauses so you can inspect the arrows.
